expectations.text: Uses the Policy API base path /policy/api/v1 for the security policy and rule calls
expectations.evidence: All calls use `$NSX/policy/api/v1/infra/domains/default/...`; section titled '3. API path (Policy API)'.

expectations.text: Does NOT present the Manager API /api/v1 as a valid surface for creating policy objects
expectations.evidence: Manager API is never offered for policy object creation; only `/api/session/*` is used outside `/policy/api/v1`.

expectations.text: Auth uses POST /api/session/create with form fields j_username and j_password
States that BOTH the JSESSIONID cookie AND the X-XSRF-TOKEN header must be sent on subsequent calls
expectations.evidence: Contradicts itself: 'Every subsequent call then needs **both** the cookie and the token' is undercut ~15 lines later by 'The XSRF token is only required for state-changing verbs (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), but sending it on GETs too is harmless.' The cookie is also never named JSESSIONID; only a cookie jar (-c/-b /tmp/nsx-cookies.txt) is used.

expectations.text: Creates or references a security policy under a domain before creating the rule (correct nesting, not a bare rule POST)
expectations.evidence: Section 4 PATCHes `/infra/domains/default/security-policies/block-rdp-app-to-db` with the rule nested in a `rules` array — 'A `PATCH` against the security policy path creates the section and its rule together.'

expectations.text: States the prerequisite that both source and destination groups must already exist and be referenced by path
expectations.evidence: Section 2 'Find the exact paths of your two groups' — 'Don't guess the group IDs ... You're looking for the `path` field', plus a warning that groups absent from the listing are VPC-scoped.

expectations.text: Explicitly labels the answer as applying to VCF 9.1 / NSX 9.1
expectations.evidence: Title: 'Blocking RDP (tcp/3389) app-tier -> db-tier with the NSX Policy API (VCF 9.1)'.

expectations.text: Includes the caveat that the skill was built from documentation and not validated against a live environment
expectations.evidence: No caveat that the answer is documentation-derived and unvalidated. The closest statement is the opposite in tone: 'has been stable across NSX 3.x through the NSX bundled with VCF 9.x, so these calls should work as written on 9.1.'

expectations.text: Contains no endpoint that is absent from the 9.1 nsx_policy_api spec
expectations.evidence: All cited paths present in 9.1__nsx-policy.ops.json: ReadIntentStatus (/infra/realized-state/status), GetGroupVMMembers (/infra/domains/{d}/groups/{g}/members/virtual-machines), ListServicesForTenant, PatchSecurityRule, DeleteSecurityPolicyForDomain.

notes: without_skill: 'when you supply `service_entries`, you set `services` to `["ANY"]`' is asserted as a requirement; no spec or dossier source establishes this coupling. The with_skill answer omits `services` entirely, which matches the Rule schema.
without_skill claims XSRF is 'only required for state-changing verbs' — not supported by any source in the research corpus.
